subproblem.title: Ambient line derivative of a locally Lipschitz map along a differentiable chart (Simon Ch. 2, (4.7), (4.10); parent Step 5)
subproblem.statement: Let n, N, p ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝᴺ open, f : ℝᴺ → ℝᵖ locally Lipschitz on U, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ and u ∈ ℝⁿ, with ψ(u) ∈ U, ψ differentiable at u and f∘ψ differentiable at u. Then for every w ∈ ℝⁿ the map t ↦ f(ψ(u) + t·Dψ(u)w) has derivative D(f∘ψ)(u)w at t = 0, i.e. HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u w) (ψ u) (fderiv ℝ ψ u w).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N p : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn p) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N) (u : Rn n), IsOpen U → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → ψ u ∈ U → DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ u → DifferentiableAt ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u → ∀ w : Rn n, HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u w) (ψ u) (fderiv ℝ ψ u w)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Step 5: Simon, Ch. 2, (4.7) and (4.10) (chapter-02.txt ≈ lines 922–957, printed pp. 56–57). The derivative of f along the chart curve γ(t) = ψ(u + tw) is compared with the derivative along the straight line γ̃(t) = ψ(u) + t·Dψ(u)w, using the local Lipschitz bound of f on the open set U. Both curves pass through ψ(u) with velocity Dψ(u)w. Simon's ψ is C¹, but only differentiability of ψ at u is used here, and injectivity of Dψ(u) is not needed. All Mathlib names refer to the pinned snapshot and are available after `import GMT.Ch03.Submission`.

Fix w ∈ ℝⁿ and put x := ψ(u), τ := Dψ(u)w (= fderiv ℝ ψ u w) and ℓ := D(f∘ψ)(u)w (= fderiv ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u w).

1. The goal as a little-o statement. By definition, HasLineDerivAt ℝ f ℓ x τ means that t ↦ f(x + t·τ) has derivative ℓ at t = 0. Equivalently (`hasLineDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero`): f(x + tτ) − f(x) − tℓ = o(t) as t → 0 (t ∈ ℝ).

2. A Lipschitz neighbourhood of x. Since x = ψ(u) ∈ U and f is locally Lipschitz on U, there are L ≥ 0 and T ∈ 𝓝[U] x such that f is L-Lipschitz on T. As U is open and x ∈ U, 𝓝[U] x = 𝓝 x (`IsOpen.nhdsWithin_eq`), so T is a neighbourhood of x.

3. Line derivatives of ψ and of f∘ψ at u in direction w. ψ is differentiable at u with derivative Dψ(u). The chain rule with the affine map t ↦ u + tw (`HasFDerivAt.hasLineDerivAt`) gives HasLineDerivAt ℝ ψ τ u w, i.e.
 (a) ψ(u + tw) − ψ(u) − tτ = o(t) as t → 0.
 Likewise f∘ψ is differentiable at u with derivative D(f∘ψ)(u), so HasLineDerivAt ℝ (f∘ψ) ℓ u w, i.e.
 (b) f(ψ(u + tw)) − f(ψ(u)) − tℓ = o(t) as t → 0.

4. Both curves eventually lie in T. The map t ↦ u + tw is continuous with value u at t = 0, and ψ is continuous at u because it is differentiable there. So ψ(u + tw) → ψ(u) = x as t → 0. Also x + tτ → x as t → 0, by continuity of t ↦ x + tτ. Since T is a neighbourhood of x, there is a neighbourhood of 0 in ℝ on which both ψ(u + tw) ∈ T and x + tτ ∈ T.

5. Comparison of the two curves (Simon (4.7)). For t in that neighbourhood, the Lipschitz bound on T (`LipschitzOnWith.norm_sub_le`) gives
 ‖f(x + tτ) − f(ψ(u + tw))‖ ≤ L·‖(x + tτ) − ψ(u + tw)‖ = L·‖ψ(u + tw) − ψ(u) − tτ‖.
 The equality holds because the two vectors are negatives of each other (x = ψ(u)). Hence f(x + tτ) − f(ψ(u + tw)) = O(ψ(u + tw) − ψ(u) − tτ) as t → 0 (`Asymptotics.IsBigO.of_bound`). By (a) and `Asymptotics.IsBigO.trans_isLittleO`,
 (c) f(x + tτ) − f(ψ(u + tw)) = o(t) as t → 0.

6. Conclusion. For every t ∈ ℝ, using x = ψ(u),
 f(x + tτ) − f(x) − tℓ = [f(x + tτ) − f(ψ(u + tw))] + [f(ψ(u + tw)) − f(ψ(u)) − tℓ].
 The two brackets are o(t) by (c) and (b), so their sum is o(t) (`Asymptotics.IsLittleO.add`, `Asymptotics.IsLittleO.congr_left`). By step 1 this is HasLineDerivAt ℝ f ℓ x τ, i.e. HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u w) (ψ u) (fderiv ℝ ψ u w). Since w ∈ ℝⁿ was arbitrary, the claim holds for every w. (For w = 0, in particular when n = 0, τ = 0 and ℓ = 0, and the statement is the derivative of a constant function; the argument covers this case.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Rewrite the goal HasLineDerivAt ℝ f ℓ x τ, with x = ψ u, τ = Dψ(u)w and ℓ = D(f∘ψ)(u)w, as f(x + tτ) − f(x) − tℓ = o(t) (hasLineDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero).
U is open and f is locally Lipschitz on U, so f is L-Lipschitz on a neighbourhood T of x.
Chain rule along t ↦ u + tw (HasFDerivAt.hasLineDerivAt): ψ(u + tw) − ψ(u) − tτ = o(t) and f(ψ(u + tw)) − f(ψ(u)) − tℓ = o(t).
For t near 0, both ψ(u + tw) and x + tτ lie in T, so ‖f(x + tτ) − f(ψ(u + tw))‖ ≤ L‖ψ(u + tw) − ψ(u) − tτ‖ = o(t) (Simon (4.7)).
Adding the two o(t) terms gives f(x + tτ) − f(x) − tℓ = o(t), which is the HasLineDerivAt claim, for every w.

subproblem.title: Rademacher's theorem for maps locally Lipschitz on an open subset of ℝⁿ (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.4 localized as in (4.8); parent Steps 2–4)
subproblem.statement: Let n, p ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝⁿ open and g : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ locally Lipschitz on W (every x ∈ W has a neighbourhood within W on which g is Lipschitz). Then g is (Fréchet) differentiable at Lⁿ-almost every point of W, i.e. Lⁿ({u ∈ W : g is not differentiable at u}) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n p : ℕ) (W : Set (Rn n)) (g : Rn n → Rn p), IsOpen W → LocallyLipschitzOn W g → ∀ᵐ u ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), u ∈ W → DifferentiableAt ℝ g u
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Steps 2–4: Simon, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.4 (Rademacher; chapter-02.txt ≈ lines 59–72, printed p. 40), applied locally exactly as in (4.8) (chapter-02.txt ≈ lines 932–950, printed p. 57). The local Lipschitz bound of parent Step 2 is now taken directly from the hypothesis that g is locally Lipschitz on W. All Mathlib names refer to the pinned snapshot (Mathlib 25730c7c) and are available after `import GMT.Ch03.Submission`. Here ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and Lⁿ = volume.

1. Reformulation. Let Z := {u ∈ ℝⁿ : u ∈ W and g is not differentiable at u}. The claim "for Lⁿ-a.e. u, u ∈ W ⇒ g is differentiable at u" says exactly that the set where this implication fails, which is Z, has Lⁿ-measure 0 (`MeasureTheory.ae_iff`). So it suffices to prove Lⁿ(Z) = 0.

2. A ball on which g is Lipschitz. Fix x ∈ Z; in particular x ∈ W. By the definition of `LocallyLipschitzOn W g` there are K ≥ 0 and a set T ∈ 𝓝[W] x such that g is K-Lipschitz on T. Since W is open and x ∈ W, 𝓝[W] x = 𝓝 x (`IsOpen.nhdsWithin_eq`). So T is a neighbourhood of x, and there is r > 0 with B := B_r(x) ⊆ T (`Metric.mem_nhds_iff`). Hence g is K-Lipschitz on B (`LipschitzOnWith.mono`).

3. Rademacher on B. Use Rademacher's theorem for a map that is Lipschitz on a set: Simon 1.4 applied componentwise to the Lipschitz extension of Simon 1.2, or in Mathlib `LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem`. The Mathlib lemma holds for every additive Haar measure on a finite-dimensional real normed space. In particular it holds for volume on ℝⁿ, including n = 0, where volume is the unit point mass. It gives: for Lⁿ-a.e. v, v ∈ B ⇒ g is differentiable within B at v. Equivalently (`MeasureTheory.ae_iff`), the set E_x := {v : v ∈ B and g is not differentiable within B at v} satisfies Lⁿ(E_x) = 0.

4. Z ∩ B ⊆ E_x. Let v ∈ Z ∩ B, so v ∈ B. Suppose g were differentiable within B at v. Since B is open and v ∈ B, B is a neighbourhood of v. So differentiability within B at v would imply differentiability at v (`DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt` with `Metric.isOpen_ball.mem_nhds`), contradicting v ∈ Z. Hence v ∈ E_x. Therefore Lⁿ(Z ∩ B) ≤ Lⁿ(E_x) = 0 (`MeasureTheory.measure_mono_null`).

5. Local nullity. Z ∩ B is a neighbourhood of x within Z, because B ∈ 𝓝 x (`Metric.ball_mem_nhds`, `inter_mem_nhdsWithin`). Thus every point x ∈ Z has a neighbourhood within Z of Lⁿ-measure zero.

6. Countable cover (Lindelöf). ℝⁿ is second countable. For each x ∈ Z take the neighbourhood N_x := Z ∩ B_{r(x)}(x) of step 5. `TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhdsWithin` yields a countable set {x_i} ⊆ Z with Z ⊆ ⋃_i N_{x_i}. Countable subadditivity gives Lⁿ(Z) ≤ Σ_i Lⁿ(N_{x_i}) = 0. (This is precisely `MeasureTheory.measure_null_of_locally_null` applied to Z with step 5.) Hence Lⁿ(Z) = 0, which by step 1 is the claim. (If W = ∅ then Z = ∅ and the claim is trivial; the argument covers this case.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Let Z = {u ∈ W : g is not differentiable at u}. The a.e. claim is equivalent to Lⁿ(Z) = 0 (ae_iff).
For x ∈ Z, W is open, so the neighbourhood given by LocallyLipschitzOn contains a ball B_r(x) on which g is Lipschitz.
Apply Rademacher (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem) on B_r(x). The ball is open, so differentiability within it is differentiability, hence Lⁿ(Z ∩ B_r(x)) = 0.
Every point of Z has an Lⁿ-null neighbourhood within Z. Second countability (measure_null_of_locally_null / countable_cover_nhdsWithin) then gives Lⁿ(Z) = 0.

Empty and zero-dimensional cases are covered. The proof is complete and non-circular; the bare declaration name is unreserved.
